JAZLYNN KURNIANDRA  ·  DESIGNED WITH SHAINA SAHU

1  Getting to know Shaina

Senior at Columbia Engineering, 21, building a startup. She has solved comfort versus style for herself. What she has not solved is the weather.

What the interview told me

1  Comfort, for her, is economic. She said comfort over style without hesitating, but the reason was repeat use. Shoes that hurt get worn here and there.

2  She has already resolved comfort versus style. “Most of the shoes I have at this point, they do have both.” A new pair cannot reintroduce the trade-off.

3  Ballet flats are what she reaches for, and winter takes them away. She wears sneakers or flats, says she wears flats a lot, then adds she cannot wear them as much in winter.

4  Looseness bothers her, fastening does not. Tying laces does not take long, she said, yet she asks for an adjustable tie and shoes that stay fitted.

5  Her benchmark is a shoe that stops being a decision. The plain black-and-white Samba she wears with everything. Her word for it was dependable.

The design problem

She does not need another comfortable shoe. She needs the one she already loves to survive November.

01Must-haves
  • Cushioned supportive insole
  • Reinforced toe and heel
  • Wide feet inside a slim design
  • Water-resistant, higher coverage
  • Breathable, sockless-friendly
  • Firm heel counter
  • Adjustable tie, stays fitted
02Preferences
  • Lightweight, flexible build
  • Solid colours, subtle accent
  • Low-profile, works with any outfit
  • Subtle lift from a higher sole
03Aspirations
  • Elegant ballet-flat look, but practical
  • Timeless
  • Comfortable enough to jog in
  • Non-wasteful material

2  My original design

Drawn from the interview before any AI was involved. A ballet flat with the structure of a sneaker.

What it is

  • Cross-over elastic straps, so it slips on and stays fitted
  • Breathable mesh upper with suede overlays
  • Padded heel collar and cushioned midsole
  • Rubber outsole with a little height
  • Beige, bone and burnt-orange, with a worn-in finish

Functional value

Lift, grip and coverage so the flat she already loves can be worn in wet weather. Elastic instead of laces because she wants fit without fuss.

Emotional value

She keeps things that show time passing, fifteen pairs going back to middle school, and she wants to move fast enough to feel like flying. So I built the character in at the factory.

3  The AI design

I uploaded the interview transcript and asked the AI to design a shoe for my partner. This is what it returned, unedited.

What it proposed

  • “The Everyday Classic”, a dark brown suede penny loafer
  • Cushioned insole and padded collar
  • Durable rubber outsole, slight heel lift
  • Four classic neutrals, suede and leather lining
  • Pitched for work, travel, dates and everyday comfort

What it got right

It heard the must-haves. Cushioning, a reinforced durable build, a subtle height boost and all-season wear are all on her list.

What it missed

It designed for “him”. It never read who Shaina is: it dropped the ballet flat she actually wears, chose brown over the quiet neutrals she asked for, and added a loafer she never mentioned. Generic comfort, no person in it.

4  Shaina chose the original

I sent her the AI design on 3 October and asked what she thought. Her reply, unedited, and what each line of it points to.

AI design

Original, her pick

“nooo i don’t really like how they look, idt ill get much use out of them. they’re prioritising things like versatility and height boost that i don’t really care about. the ones you designed were visually appealing and focused on comfort which i care the most about”

Shaina, iMessage, 3 October. Her first question on seeing it was “did u specify to make shoes for shaina just so it knows”: the AI had written the shoe for “him”.

Her wordsAI designMy original design
“i don’t really like how they look”A penny loafer in dark brown suede, written for “his next chapter”. She never named loafers.A ballet flat with sneaker structure, the shoe she already reaches for most.
“idt ill get much use out of them”Pitched for work, travel and dates. Suede does not like rain, so it would sit out the winter too.Coverage, grip and a water-resistant sole, so the flat stays in rotation all year.
“versatility and height boost that i don’t really care about”Leads with all-season versatility and a confidence-giving heel lift.Leads with cushioning, fit and a sockless-friendly upper. Lift is subtle and only there for wet ground.
“focused on comfort which i care the most about”Comfort is one of five equal icons.Comfort is the brief. Cushioned midsole, padded collar, elastic that keeps it fitted.
The AI optimised for versatility and height. Shaina optimises for comfort and use. She chose the one with her in it.

5  What Shaina changed

Her feedback on the original, quoted from her messages, and what each note changed in the redesign.

V1Original

Ballet-flat and sneaker hybrid. Elastic straps, mesh and suede, padded collar, worn-in finish, beige and burnt-orange.

What she told me to change

“the only thing i would change is i don’t love the sporty look, like id want it too look more sleek/feminine/polished”

Changed

The sneaker upper came off. Version 2 is a true ballet-flat last with a bow at the toe. The sporty language is cut to one tonal panel line.

“also tbh i do like a worn in look but i do like how new shoes look neat and clean hahaha”

Changed

The worn-in finish is gone. I had read her kept old shoes as wanting the wear printed in. She would rather the shoe start clean and earn it.

“i don’t really have one but you can do a cream/off white so it goes w many things”

Changed

Beige, bone and burnt-orange out. Cream and off-white in. One quiet colour does more work than a two-tone scheme.

V2Co-created redesign

A true ballet flat. Bow at the toe, gathered topline, one reduced panel, a stacked water-resistant sole, and her name on the footbed where only she sees it.

Version 1 was my reading of Shaina. Version 2 is the part she corrected

6  The co-created design, annotated

Function, emotional value, and why each part is better for Shaina than the version she sent back

1Ballet-flat last, bow at the toe
Function

Slips on without laces, in a flat silhouette rather than a sneaker shell.

Emotion

Put together rather than sporty, which is how she said she wants to look.

Why better

Version 1 was a hybrid trainer. She asked for sleek and feminine, so the sneaker shell came off.

2Cream and off-white colourway
Function

One tonal colour across upper, panel and sole.

Emotion

A shoe she never has to think about in the morning.

Why better

Burnt-orange was my guess. She named cream herself, so the colour is her decision now.

3Reduced quarter panel
Function

Reinforcement across the flex zone, where a flat creases first.

Emotion

Reads as structure, not branding.

Why better

Cut to one tonal line. Closest to the sporty note she flagged, so it is first to test with her.

4Stacked, water-resistant sole
Function

Subtle lift off wet ground, with grip for city walking.

Emotion

Ends the half of the year her favourite shoe sits in the cupboard.

Why better

The one problem she could not solve herself. Her flats are summer-only; this makes them February shoes.

5Gathered elastic topline
Function

Adjustable hold so the flat does not loosen with wear.

Emotion

Fits without fuss, which matters to someone optimising her day.

Why better

Slimmer than Version 1's padded collar, so the polished line she asked for survives.

6Her name on the footbed
Function

The mark sits inside the shoe, hidden once it is on.

Emotion

A private reminder, not an announcement.

Why better

Version 1 put a symbol on the heel. She does not want distractions, so it moved inside.

The shoe must let Shaina stay polished and stay out, in the same pair, in February
